summary:
The Astronaut Health Monitoring System is a web-based prototype designed to organize and display important health information of astronauts during space missions. It provides a centralized dashboard to monitor selected health indicators such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, and body temperature.

The website includes a dashboard for viewing sample health readings, a demo login interface, threshold-based alerts to highlight unusual sample values, and a history section to review previous readings.

This project addresses the challenge of presenting astronaut health information in a clear and organized way, especially in the demanding environment of space where access to ordinary medical facilities is limited. By bringing important health indicators together in one place, the prototype demonstrates how web technologies can support mission health awareness and monitoring.

Currently, the system uses simulated data for demonstration purposes. Future improvements could include real-time sensor integration, secure data storage, and advanced health trend analysis.
details: Astronaut Health Monitoring System is a web-based prototype for simulated space missions. What it does: Shows an astronaut's sample heart rate (BPM), oxygen saturation (%) and body temperature (°C) together on one dashboard. How it works: A demo login opens the dashboard. JavaScript checks each reading against demo thresholds and shows a status or alert message. Earlier readings are saved and can be viewed in a history page. Benefits: Health readings are easy to review in one place instead of scattered across records. The layout is simple and works on mobile and desktop. Intended impact: An educational demo of how mission health data can be organised and presented. It can be expanded with real sensors later. Tools used: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and browser Local Storage (optional) for demo records. Creativity: One simple dashboard that combines readings, alerts and history, built with only basic web technologies. Factors considered: Clarity, ease of use, responsive design, and clear limits. All data is simulated, and it gives no medical diagnosis.
